# Results on one page

**System.** A Java 21 / Spring Boot service streams NASA C-MAPSS FD001 readings (a simulated turbofan benchmark)
through Kafka. It keeps a sliding window per engine, scores remaining useful life with an in-process ONNX model and
raises de-duplicated alerts.

**Pre-registered question.** Do the 8 sensors ranked highest by correlation with RUL predict as well as all 21?
Non-inferiority margin {{ n.margin }} cycle of test RMSE, {{ n.n_seeds }} seeds, {{ n.split_test }} held-out engines.

| gradient boosting, 21 sensors (shipped) | {{ n.main_gbr_full21_test_rmse }} ± {{ n.main_gbr_full21_test_rmse_std }} |
| gradient boosting, 15 informative sensors | {{ n.main_gbr_informative15_test_rmse }} ± {{ n.main_gbr_informative15_test_rmse_std }} |
| gradient boosting, 8 ranked sensors | {{ n.main_gbr_reduced8_test_rmse }} ± {{ n.main_gbr_reduced8_test_rmse_std }} |

**Verdict: rejected.** The gap is {{ n.hyp_gap }} cycles, above the margin. The service ships all 21 sensors.

**Post hoc** (designed after the result, labelled as such):

* Which 8 matters. Forward selection on validation: +{{ n.greedy8_gap }}. Lowest-ranked 8: +{{ n.worst8_gap }}.
  Random 8: +{{ n.random8_best_gap }} to +{{ n.random8_worst_gap }}. The ranked 8 are redundant (mean correlation
  {{ n.redundancy_reduced8 }}).
* The recipe is as large as the effect. The window length moves the 21-sensor error by {{ n.window_effect_full21 }}
  cycles; the sensor gap is {{ n.gap_w10 }} / {{ n.hyp_gap }} / {{ n.gap_w60 }} at windows of 10 / 30 / 60 readings.
